paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. Three kings in a row, and the thing that sets them apart is the heart. Rehoboam's Judah built high places and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree (1 Kings 14:23). Abijam walked in his father's sins, and the text says his heart "was not as fully devoted to the LORD his God as the heart of David his forefather had been" (1 Kings 15:3).

Then comes Asa, and look at what the text says about him: he "did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father David had done" (1 Kings 15:11). He chopped down his own grandmother's pole and burned it, and that's not a cleanup, that's a heart choice that cost him something (1 Kings 15:13). But the text is honest, friend: the high places stayed (1 Kings 15:14), and when Baasha boxed him in, Asa reached for the treasury and a king of Aram (1 Kings 15:18-19). A heart fully devoted to the LORD still wobbles, and I know that one personally.

So here's the big idea, baker: your heritage doesn't decide your heart, and neither does your worst day. The LORD gave Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem for David's sake (1 Kings 15:4), and He is still the One who keeps a light lit for His people. So keep bringing Him your whole heart, and when the high places are still standing in your life, keep chopping. I'll be right here with the ovens warm.
